newsitem.title: UK: GrandMet firms after AGM comments.
newsitem.headline: GrandMet firms after AGM comments.

text.p: Shares in Grand Metropolitan Plc edged higher on Tuesday after upbeat comments from the company at its annual general meeting.
The stock was up 8-1/2p at 462 by 1135 GMT after being up 5-1/2p shortly before details of its AGM comments were released.
The company said overall spirits volumes in the first four months of the year were ahead of last year and that first-half profits would show an improvement despite the strong pound.
Chairman George Bull said trading had been as expected in the first four months of the year, with the three core businesses all trading at least in line with peers "and in many cases better."
He said Burger King had continued to outperform its major competitors with "positive comparable store sales growth," while momentum at the spirits unit IDV had continued.
Bull blamed currency factors for recent weakness in GrandMet shares, pointing out that a one cent gain in sterling against the dollar reduced profits on translation by four million stg.
"They are saying that profits are up on last year and it is difficult to argue with that," said one analyst, "but I would want to know more about volumes in Pillsbury and in IDV."
"The statement sounds good," the analyst said, "but Grand Met has flattered to deceive so many times before, it all sounds so much better than it actually turns out."
By 1218 GMT the stock had eased off it's highs to be up 5-1/2p at 459.
